title: Mint the pro-rata-ratio lesson as its own id (folded into L-214 at the 52/52 cap)
why: register cap -- the lessons register was at 52/52 entries during the Release 1 window, so a genuinely distinct lesson was folded into L-214 rather than minting a new id; archiving to make room is a deliberate cross-reference-checked process that should not be rushed during a release
notes: The folded rule is separate and expensive: a pro-rata ratio must be derived from the SPECIFIC stored row being reversed, never a sum across the parent entity's rows. The class hides because the CLOSING operation books the exact remaining and absorbs the difference, so the total always reconciles and the error surfaces only as filing-PERIOD attribution, and only when a partial straddles a boundary. Cost of leaving it folded: the register's value is that a future session can find a rule by its own id and citation, and a distinct lesson living inside another entry is materially less discoverable. Action: archive the least-cited fully-guarded entry properly, then mint this as its own id. Rationale for the interim fold is recorded in .claude/lessons/_meta.json note.

title: Code-map catch-up: 42 code commits merged to master since the last map refresh (a76e2e2c..c73b0897)
why: release throughput -- every lane merged under Bookkeeping Option B, which defers the map entry to a docs-only follow-up after the code PR lands; the follow-ups have not kept pace with the Release 1 merge rate, so the debt is now 42 commits across api, web, mobile and packages
notes: Range a76e2e2c..c73b0897, 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-22, spanning #1048 through #1212. Surfaced by the stop gate firing on a docs-only branch off master: the gate compares code commits against the last .claude/code-map/ change, so the debt is inherited by every branch cut from master and every lane now trips it regardless of whether that lane mapped its own work. Not any one lane's to absorb -- mapping 42 other PRs from outside their context is how a map gets confidently wrong. Owned by the landing coordinator, which works from a master tree and owns bookkeeping. Note that the gate's own remedy text (the Bookkeeping-Follow-Up trailer) is what allowed the debt to accumulate silently: it is per-PR and has no aggregate ceiling, so consider whether the gate should also fail on a backlog depth rather than only on the presence of a trailer. OBSERVED RECURRENCE (same session): this gate has now fired THREE times on a docs-only branch that contains no code at all, each time listing the same 99 unmapped files from other lanes' merges. That is direct evidence for the second finding above -- the check is branch-relative, so the complaint is inherited by every branch cut from master and carries no information about the lane seeing it. Each firing was satisfied by the Bookkeeping-Follow-Up trailer, which is exactly the loop described: the only available response to a noisy signal is the escape hatch, and the escape hatch is what lets the debt grow. A gate whose remedy is reached for reflexively has stopped being a gate. Suggested shape for the fix: compare against the map state of the branch's MERGE-BASE rather than its tip, so a branch is only asked about code IT introduced. PROVENANCE: the 42-commit figure is `git log --oneline a76e2e2c..c73b0897 -- apps/ packages/ scripts/ | wc -l`, run 2026-09-22 by the MacBook lane. The three-firings observation is first-hand, from this session's own stop-hook output.

title: Mint the verification-asymmetry lesson as its own id (pairs with D-24)
why: register cap -- the lessons register is at 52/52 during the Release 1 window, same constraint as D-24; mint both in one pass once an entry is properly archived post-release
notes: THE RULE: a verification framed as 'is my work safe' is answered the moment your own side passes, so it stops there by construction. Frame it as 'did this change weaken anything', which is symmetric and cannot be answered without checking BOTH sides. Concretely for a merge: revert YOUR change on the merged tree and confirm your cases still fail, then revert THEIRS and confirm theirs still fail. EVIDENCE: on the #1219/#1221 merge rehearsal the forward probe passed and the reverse probe found that #1221's fix had no guard in the DEFAULT Jest lane -- reverting only the fix on the merged tree left all 395 unit tests green. CORRECTION (2026-09-22, after this row was first written): I also repeated a stronger claim that no CI workflow runs the DB lane. That is FALSE and I should not have carried it without checking the triggers myself. db-migrations.yml DOES run `npm run test:db -w apps/api` (line 143), path-gated, and one of its trigger paths is `apps/api/src/**/*.db.spec.ts` -- so it fired for #1221 precisely because that PR added a .db.spec.ts. The accurate and more interesting gap: a PR that changes SERVICE LOGIC an existing DB spec covers, without touching any filtered path, never re-triggers that workflow -- the guard runs when someone ADDS a test, not when someone CHANGES the thing the test protects. The default-lane pin is still the right remedy, for that narrower reason. Two independent reviews had passed it; both were right about everything they checked, and neither was scoped to ask whether the guard EXECUTES where regressions are caught. SECOND RULE, same incident: a missing guard is silent in the direction that matters -- the suite runs green, the diff contains tests, the test-file count goes UP, so every signal points the right way and no observation available to a PR reviewer distinguishes a guard from a file shaped like one. The remedy is structural, not 'review harder': a fix whose guard is a DB-lane spec must ALSO carry a default-lane pin of the same behaviour, because the DB spec proves it against real transactions while the unit pin proves it still exists. Worked example: #1221's added pin. THIRD RULE, from how this row itself went wrong. The operational form, which is checkable WHILE you write rather than after: COULD A LATER READER DISPROVE THIS ROW IN UNDER A MINUTE, AND DOES THE ROW TELL THEM WHERE TO LOOK? If not, it is an assertion, not a fact. In practice that means carrying how the claim was established -- the command, the file and line, or the name of whoever checked it. 'Record provenance' states the goal; this test tells you when you have met it. Once written down, a claim someone VERIFIED and a claim someone RELAYED look identical; the register records what is believed, not how it came to be believed, so a later reader has no handle to re-check. This row originally carried a false CI claim that the author had relayed from a colleague's report while writing it as though first-hand -- the same shape as its own second rule, one level up. 'No workflow runs the DB lane' is unfalsifiable by a later reader; 'verified 2026-09-22 by reading db-migrations.yml triggers and line 143' invites exactly the check that catches it. PROVENANCE for this row's own claims: the db-migrations.yml trigger and step were read directly by the MacBook lane on 2026-09-22; the 395-to-389 probe figures are first-hand from running the default lane with the service change reverted on the merged tree. FOURTH RULE, same shape, cheapest of the four: a message asserting a CLOCK time carries the output of `date -u` rather than an estimate, and a message asserting ELAPSED time is a proxy by construction and should not be asserted at all. A stated time is stale on arrival -- only the command is durable. EVIDENCE (first-hand, this session, 2026-09-22): the fleet lead stated 09:00Z when it was 08:34Z, then 09:05Z when it was 09:35Z; `date -u` on the MacBook read 09:37:48Z, by which point even the correction was two minutes stale. WHY IT BELONGS WITH THE OTHERS RATHER THAN IN A CARE-MORE NOTE: these errors were committed BY the people running the conversation about this exact error class, WHILE running it. That is evidence it is not an attention failure and will not yield to resolving to be careful. Everything genuinely fixed on 2026-09-22 was structural -- the sha gate resolving against origin instead of string-matching, the default-lane pin requirement, merge-base comparison for the code-map gate. None of it was fixed by anyone trying harder.
